tasks.short: Analyse soil microorganisms and chemical relationships

steps.what: Define the microbial reaction or chemical-mineralogical question, verify soil sample provenance and select appropriate chemical analysis methods and controls.
Perform the chemical analyses of soil microorganism content, prepare controls and capture actual assay readings and observations in the laboratory notebook system {OTHER}.

Calculate concentration, blank corrections and chosen summary comparisons using validated native {SPREADSHEET} tables and plots; inspect sample alignment, units and controls before accepting the calculation output.

Interpret the microbial reactions or chemical-mineralogical relationships to plant growth and write the final analysis record with method limits and competing explanations; check it against all source evidence.
Save the checked final soil analysis record in the laboratory notebook system {OTHER}.

tasks.design: Configure validated native calculation and plot tables in {SPREADSHEET}, retaining sample references to the laboratory notebook system {OTHER}. The scientist performs the chemistry and determines what the results say about soils and plant growth.
tasks.previous_blocker: The same assay arithmetic and sample plots were rebuilt for each run.
tasks.enabler_now: Native formula tables can reuse explicit sample IDs, units and control references.
tasks.still_hard: Microbial activity, soil heterogeneity and plant response do not reduce to a concentration formula.
tasks.human_edge: Separate a measured association from a supported biological explanation.

ambition.what: No new causal or agronomic decision authority.

tasks.altitude: Less repeated assay arithmetic; the same laboratory and scientific work remains.

evidence.claim: Native spreadsheet formula tables and plots can reuse explicit assay inputs while scientific interpretation stays human.

assumptions: Boundary includes the scientist's chemical analysis through its laboratory record, not a field recommendation. Shares are a scenario, not observed timings.

The scientist captures sample ID, site and depth, collection date, method revision, assay reading and unit, dilution, blank, replicate and control flag in s1-s2. Manual source entry and checking remain counted; instrument exports are optional existing inputs. Missing values are investigated or retained as missing, never imputed silently.

Native spreadsheet and notebook functions are tested before code. Only repeated arithmetic and plotting setup lose time. Wet-laboratory work, source capture, interpretation and actual record writing are retained.
The ordinary author check in s4 covers the final record saved at s5. Any edited value or conclusion invalidates it.
unknowns: Usability of existing sample and instrument exports
research_questions: Can native tables preserve method revision and control flags through the plots?

already_counted.description: Check assay calculation inputs, controls and plots.

incremental.description: Validate calculation tables when analytical methods change.

approvals.approved_version: Final soil analysis record checked at the end of s4

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Where repeated assay arithmetic and plots occupy 20 hours, native reuse removes 35%: 7 gross hours less 1.5 upkeep. Zero when already configured. Physical analysis and scientific interpretation remain fully retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Develop soil alterations for particular plants

steps.what: Examine the soil profile, existing test results and plant requirements; identify the actual constraints on growth and the available amendment evidence.
Develop candidate ways of altering the soil and design bounded trials, considering pH, structure, drainage, salinity and plant tolerance rather than applying a generic recipe.
Carry out the soil alteration trials, observe the actual soil and plant response and capture treatment, timing and adverse effects.
Compare trial observations and write the final method findings; use native {SPREADSHEET} treatment tables and unit formulas, retaining all scientific selection, interpretation and final checking.
Save the checked final soil alteration findings in {DOCS}.

tasks.design: Reuse native treatment-comparison tables in {SPREADSHEET} and store the scientist's checked findings in {DOCS}. Candidate soil alterations and their trials remain human research; only repeated table setup and unit arithmetic change.
tasks.previous_blocker: Trial comparison tables were repeatedly rebuilt despite the same treatment and observation structure.
tasks.enabler_now: Native spreadsheet tables can reuse columns and explicit unit formulas.
tasks.still_hard: A soil amendment can help one plant and harm another, with effects dependent on the actual site.
tasks.human_edge: Choose and interpret trials that address the plant's real constraints.
tasks.altitude: The research week changes little beyond a small reduction in comparison preparation.

evidence.claim: Native treatment tables can reuse observation columns and unit arithmetic without choosing a soil amendment.

assumptions: Boundary is developing and testing a soil alteration method through its findings record. Full-scale farm application and advice distribution are separate. Shares are illustrative.

The scientist captures trial ID, plot or pot ID, plant type, soil source, treatment, dose and unit, actual application date, control, response observation and adverse effect in s2-s3. The laboratory notebook system {OTHER} holds actual trial notes. Manual entry and verification are retained; absent responses remain missing.

Native tables are tested first. Only table structure and arithmetic reuse reduce s4; all actual soil examination, method design, trials, scientific interpretation and prose remain counted. Results from another task are source inputs, not a second calculation saving.
s4's ordinary author check covers the final findings saved in s5. Changes invalidate it. No extra reporting obligation is introduced.
unknowns: Current time spent on comparison setup
research_questions: Can the existing table preserve treatment and observation units without manual relabelling?

already_counted.description: Interpret actual trial observations and check final findings.

incremental.description: Maintain the small treatment table and unit formulas.

approvals.approved_version: Final soil alteration findings checked at the end of s4

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Native table setup removes 15% of the existing 14-hour comparison and record share: 2.1 gross hours less 0.5 upkeep. Zero with reusable tables already in place. Research and trials retain all 85 hours.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Experiment on soil formation and ecosystem interactions

steps.what: Choose the soil formation, change or ecosystem-interaction question and design the experiment, controls, sampling plan and observation methods.
Conduct the experiment, maintain treatments and controls, collect actual soil and organism observations, and record deviations in the laboratory or field notebook system {OTHER}.
Prepare observation summaries and plots in {SPREADSHEET}; configure native tables and charts to reuse the selected experimental factors, checking missing observations, control alignment and units.
Interpret the soil formation, change or organism interactions and write and check the final experiment conclusions, including deviations and limits to causal claims.
Save the checked final soil experiment record in the laboratory or field notebook system {OTHER}.

tasks.design: Reuse native summary tables and charts in {SPREADSHEET} from actual experiment observations held in the notebook system {OTHER}. Experimental design, execution and scientific conclusions remain with the scientist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated factor and observation plots were set up manually after each experiment.
tasks.enabler_now: Native tables and chart configurations can reuse explicit factor and observation columns.
tasks.still_hard: Long-term ecosystem effects, uncontrolled variation and causal interpretation remain research problems.
tasks.human_edge: Design meaningful controls and recognise when the experiment cannot resolve the question.
tasks.altitude: A small reduction in summary preparation leaves the field and experimental role intact.

evidence.claim: Native spreadsheet tables can regenerate factor-based summaries from actual observation rows.

assumptions: Boundary is a soil formation or ecosystem experiment, distinct from the chemical assay and amendment trials in sibling tasks. No duplicated underlying experimental work is credited. Shares are illustrative.

The scientist produces experiment ID, site or sample ID, treatment, control, observation time, measured variable, value, unit, method and deviation in s1-s2. Actual capture remains counted. Manual entry is the fallback; a scheduled observation never becomes a completed measurement automatically.

Native tables and notebook export features are tried before code. Only repeated summary construction loses time; experimental execution, observation capture, scientific interpretation and final record writing are unchanged.
The ordinary final record check in s4 approves the exact s5 snapshot. Any amended data or conclusion requires recheck.
research_questions: Can native summaries retain missingness and experimental controls without reshaping source notes manually?

already_counted.description: Check experiment summary construction and observation alignment.

incremental.description: Maintain factor and observation table configurations.

approvals.approved_version: Final soil experiment record checked at the end of s4

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Summary reuse removes 40% of the 10-hour summary share: 4 gross hours less 1 upkeep. Zero with native summaries already configured. No fieldwork or experiment runtime saving is claimed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan composting or farming waste management

steps.what: Assess the composting or farming site's actual waste streams, quantities, contamination, storage and land-use constraints, and read the applicable programme requirements.
Design the waste management programme for composting or farming, choosing segregation, treatment, monitoring and responsibilities with the site operators.
Compare material balances, storage capacity and programme costs using native {SPREADSHEET} tables; reuse explicit quantities and formulas while checking units and assumptions.
Write and check the completed waste management plan, responsibilities, monitoring limits and calculation assumptions; approve the final version and intended site-operator audience.
Save the checked final waste management plan in {DOCS}.
Send the exact stored waste management plan to the checked site-operator recipients through {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: Configure native material-balance and cost tables in {SPREADSHEET} for the scientist's chosen waste programme. The scientist retains site assessment, programme design and final plan writing in {DOCS}, followed by separate save and send actions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Programme alternatives repeatedly rebuilt the same quantity, capacity and cost arithmetic.
tasks.enabler_now: Native tables can recalculate explicit quantities and unit costs without selecting a waste treatment.
tasks.still_hard: Contamination, local constraints and operator capability determine whether a plan is workable.
tasks.human_edge: Choose a feasible programme and communicate its operational limitations.

ambition.what: No new waste-treatment or permit authority.

tasks.altitude: Less repeated arithmetic; programme decisions and site responsibilities stay with people.

evidence.claim: Native spreadsheet tables can calculate material balances and costs from explicit quantities and unit assumptions.

assumptions: This is a planning instance of the task's plan-or-supervise alternatives. Boundary ends at the delivered plan; actual site supervision and waste operations remain separate unchanged work. Shares are a scenario.

The scientist verifies waste stream ID, actual quantity and unit, contamination observation, storage capacity, treatment assumption, cost basis and monitoring requirement in s1-s3. Existing operators supply actual site records during the current assessment; manual capture and clarification are retained. Missing quantities are investigated, not invented.

Test native calculation tables first. Only repeat arithmetic and table setup lose time; site work, operator discussions, plan writing and legal applicability judgement remain fully counted. No measured waste or environmental benefit is claimed.
s4's normal author check binds the completed plan and recipients for s5-s6. Edits invalidate both approvals. Delivery is not a permit application or approval to operate.
unknowns: Reliability of waste quantities and cost inputs
research_questions: Can the native comparison table expose all capacity and unit assumptions for operator review?

incremental.description: Maintain quantity, capacity and cost-table formulas.

approvals.approved_version: Final waste management plan checked at the end of s4
Same final plan snapshot and site-operator recipients checked at the end of s4, unchanged by s5

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Native tables remove 30% of the 15-hour calculation share: 4.5 gross hours less 1 upkeep. Zero if already configured. Full plan writing and the one-hour save and send steps are retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Soil and plant scientists retain laboratory, field and programme judgement while native tables reduce repeated calculations.
reach: Clarify field observation protocols with agricultural technicians
role.ambitious_version: Make soil and plant research easier to reproduce without substituting software for field evidence or scientific judgement.
